edits.text: When the user asks for information about a product by name, you must first call list_all_product_types to find its product_id before calling get_product_details.
edits.reason: Prevents the agent from hallucinating product details by ensuring it retrieves the correct product_id before searching for specific variant information.

edits.text: When the user asks to switch a product to the cheapest available option, you must call get_product_details for that product type, identify all variants where 'available' is true, and select the one with the lowest price.
edits.reason: Fixes a logic error where the agent failed to filter for availability or correctly identify the lowest price among available options.

edits.text: When proposing a modification to a pending order, you must verify that the selected item matches all of the user's stated requirements (e.g., product type, material, color, capacity) from the product's variants before presenting it to the user.
edits.reason: Ensures the agent correctly filters available options based on all user-specified constraints instead of selecting the first match.

edits.text: When the user asks to exchange an item from one order for an item in another order, you must only perform the modification on the order the user wants to receive the item in and include both the item to be replaced and the replacement item in that modification call.
edits.reason: Prevents double-writes and ensures that an exchange between two different orders is handled as a single modification of the destination order.

dropped_by_checks.reason:
check D: User: "I want to exchange the bike in my pending order #B for the helmet in my delivered order #A. I want to receive the helmet in order #B."

The policy allows the agent to modify pending orders and exchange delivered orders. Since both actions are allowed, the agent should perform both: exchanging the helmet in order #A for the bike, and modifying the bike in order #B for the helmet. However, the rule states that the agent must "only perform the modification on the order the user wants to receive the item in" (order #B). This causes the agent to skip the modification/exchange for order #A, even though the policy allows it. This is a problem of forbidding what the policy allows (D). | D: A user has a pending order (#P1) and a delivered order (#D1). The user says, "I want to exchange the item in my pending order (#P1) for the item in my delivered order (#D1)." The user wants to receive the item in order #P1. According to the rule, the agent must ONLY perform the modification on order #P1 (the order the user wants to receive the item in). Consequently, the agent would refuse to perform the exchange on the delivered order #D1. However, the policy allows the agent to modify pending orders AND to exchange delivered orders. Since the policy allows both actions and does not forbid performing both in response to a single request, the rule's "only" restriction forbids a policy-allowed action.
